title: Render Tree
definition: The Render Tree is a combination of the DOM and CSSOM. It represents exactly what will be drawn to the screen. It only includes nodes that are visible.
simpleExplanation: The DOM knows every HTML tag that exists. The CSSOM knows every style rule. The Render Tree is the final boss. It combines them both. If the DOM has a `<div>`, but the CSSOM says `display: none`, that `<div>` is completely excluded from the Render Tree because the screen doesn't need to paint it.
realWorldExample: This is why `display: none` is good for performance when hiding huge chunks of a webpage. The browser literally ignores them when calculating the Render Tree.

basic: What two trees combine to form the Render Tree?
intermediate: If an element has `visibility: hidden;`, is it included in the Render Tree?

answers.question: visibility: hidden included?
answers.answer: YES! `visibility: hidden` makes an element invisible, but it still physically takes up empty space on the screen. Therefore, the browser must include it in the Render Tree to calculate the layout. Only `display: none` completely removes it.

codeExample:
You cannot see me, and I take up zero space.

You cannot see me, but I am still holding my empty space!

The Render Tree only cares about geometry. If it takes up space, it's in the tree.
